Name: Methane
Summary: Per-second sensor data from an underground coal mine for predicting dangerous methane concentrations at longwalls, set up as classification and regression tasks.
Description:
Coal mining is hazardous work. This dataset gathers raw sensor data from an underground coal mine so that models can learn to predict dangerous methane concentrations at longwalls over a chosen time horizon. It was published on Mendeley Data in 2021 by researchers at the Silesian University of Technology.

Each record has a timestamp and the measurements taken every second. Two tasks are set out. In classification, a model must say whether methane at three meters, MM263, MM264 and MM256, will exceed a chosen threshold, such as 1.0, within a chosen window, for example three to six minutes ahead. In regression, it must predict the methane value itself at the selected meters.

The record includes a file that describes the attributes and a PDF of plots, next to the zipped data. It is released under CC BY 4.0.
